Suspenseful little mystery/story game that can occupy you for an evening. The gameplay is engaging due to the excellent presentation, visuals, and sound, not complexity. It's very straightforward but doesn't get repetitive because the playtime is so short. 

Others in the genre such as Papers, Please or Death and Taxes do a better job of letting story and decisions emerge naturally from subtle anomalies in the normal gameplay loop. In comparison, the story here shows up quickly and becomes the immediate and only focus. This is a rare case where I think more "filler" days spent solving normal cases would actually improve the experience.

As the developer says, it's a 3-4 hour experience with almost no replay value (unless you want a few missable achievements).

The plot is above average, the graphics are pretty solid, and the audio is well suited.

There are some teething pains, such as unskippable blurs that count as cutscenes and if you ever replay a section you'll be sitting through the exact same dialogue all over again. There's also some issues with clickable areas in some scenes and a certain technical scene being a little hard to parse, since the manual uses terminology that doesn't *quite* fit.

However, the experience was quite lovely. The technical implementation is far above average, with dynamic windows, active text scrolling, and audio cues when you scroll to a certain section of text. It's extremely well coded. I see a lot of Unity games with UI issues, but this was as solid an implementation as I've seen. Well thought out, well executed, marvelous job!

And the amount of effort for a single dev, even with the support provided, is astonishing. Making this in *only* three years is quite impressive.

I do wish it was a more dynamic experience, but that requires an astonishing amount of work. As a stepping stone to future work, this is quite excellent. I'm happy to see this particular genre of game get more entires of this quality, and I'll be keeping an eye on this developer.

Highly recommended.

A great game had it come out about a decade ago. There's nothing the game does that other games don't do in greater depth and with greater innovation and interest. Tools and mechanics are all used at a very basic level, and there's no integration of multiple tools or strategies on a case to reach a conclusion as in other games of this genre. 
For example, a truly innovative element of the game is the use of a spectrometer tool, wherein information on a sample must be looked up and entered precisely in order to derive lab results. However, the tool is only used a single time. Other games in this genre would have made it a permanent element of the game moving forward, integrating it alongside other tools and resources to solve cases. This game uses it once, then abandons the idea entirely.
There's a bomb defusal scene which is fantastic... until you realize that the information is static rather than being generated. The plot and story are ok, with some nods to the X-Files and 90s conspiracies along the way, but again nothing really new or innovative beyond what's already been done in similar games. 

In sum, this is a great demo for a game that came out in 2013, but better, more complete, more elaborate, more creative games already exist that do the same things.

reviews.review:
I love cyber sleuthing games with my favorites being Orwell, Cyber Manhunt, and Her Story. So this definitely scratched an itch for me. 

Story: Story is pretty straightforward with an overarching conspiracy you have to unravel. Honestly, its not groundbreaking but it keeps you invested. What elevates it for me is the music kicking in at certain moments to heighten tension. The soundtrack for this game is not bad. 

Forewarned the story is short with most of the negative reviews highlighting that. While I wouldve liked to have had more, I will say that I prefer games being straight to the point rather than needless filler. You can get maybe 3 hours out of this so if that is not worth 14 dollars for you, then maybe skip this.  

Gameplay: Its a typical point and click adventure using an enhanced 90s style computer interface. Aside from the usual info gathering, the puzzles are thoroughly challenging with my favorite being a bomb defusal segment that I found to be quite challenging. But in a fun way. I wouldve liked to use the tools more like the bomb defusal and chemical analyzer more than once. It wouldve added another layer of challenge to the game.


I would definitely recommend buying and experiencing this game whether it be on sale or not.
I really loved this game, game play is super fun and I don't believe it was too short at all personally. It was just the right length for the story being told!

If you think this is a game where you analyze crimes while searching for increasingly complicated data you are wrong.
If you think this is a narrative game with multiple branches and endings depending on your decisions you are wrong.

Its just a linear visual novel... and was sold to me as something different.

I almost never leave reviews, so bear with me.

I was kind of enthralled by the demo: I loved the idea of drawing connections, of looking something up in one database and comparing it to the next database and finding it on a list retrieved earlier.  Then...well, I'm [i]not[/i] going to say is "bait and switch"; I think the demo is a fair representation of the game.  But the game did go in different directions than I'd hoped: for instance, the connection-drawing is in many ways the core of the game, but there was a lot of stuff around it: dialogue choices, minigames  ("oh, look, mastermind"), occasional long cutscenes.

At its core the game is a thriller, which is not really my genre.  (There's literally a "Them", which I think is the same as "The Organization", which is what you get if you ask LLMs to summarize the thriller genre.)  I could have guessed that, probably, but there's so much that seems to pay homage to [i]The X-Files[/i] (the FBI in the 1990s, the typewritten location captions, your boss is literally named Skinner for heaven's sake), and one of the first cases you get is alien-abduction-based.  This ended up being way more "thriller" in tone than X-Files was.

But to be clear: I didn't hate it!  I wish Steam had a scale more subtle than "yes/no", because I want to give it a "qualified yes" or maybe a "no, but if it's your thing, then yes".  There's a lot to like here: the atmosphere (even if you could practically see the words "cue dramatic music" at major plot twists), the interface, even a lot of the writing and plot.  Much of the voice acting is good; I really liked Pendell and Walker; Andrews less so.  (The two coroner reports, even less.)  And the [spoiler]bomb-defusing scene[/spoiler] did a great job with the tone.

Ultimately, I don't [i]regret[/i] playing it.  I also just don't recommend it unless you're looking for a thriller.  In which case, enjoy!

Her Story meets Orwell: Always Keeping An Eye On You in "The Operator!"
Similar Games: Orwell, Unheard The Voices of Crime, Her Story, Telling Lies.

[SPOILERS AHEAD]

Premise Overview:
You, Evan Tanner, are hired as as part of the Operator Program in which you work to support field agents of the fictional FDI in solving their crimes. Except, there's a bigger evil at play than your regular homicide perpetrator or arson case.


For people who love desktop style games (such as Her Story and Telling Lies) this is a goldmine. A mixture of puzzle solving, enigmatic storytelling with a capturing atmosphere, frankly fantastic voice acting and investing gameplay, The Operator strives to keep you engaged in the progression of the main, if too short, main plot line.

While the twist is admittedly a little predictable, this is a game you can enjoy none-the-less that keeps you on edge with effective sound (such as a fantastic musical score and effects such as reverberated and slow footsteps during tense moments). It fits perfectly into the hearts of those who enjoy these types of games - such as myself.

I just wish there was more in there aside from the main story. All the cases you receive are connected, which makes sense but takes away from the realistic sense the game does actually have, and you receive a whole wanted list of criminals - of which only one appears. I would have loved a side story about one of the criminals on there who was the leader of a cult.

Now, the ending. It's cold and it slaps you in the face, quite frankly. You go through all this, discover everything Evan's been through just for it to be a swift chop and done and that just doesn't seem fair and it's a little bit of a let down to have it happen so quick.  Though, there is potential and lead for a sequel.

Regardless, I really do recommend this game. I wish it was longer and I wish there was more too it but that just encourages me to keep an eye on the developers and snap up anything else they come out with.
